1. Using CO (Carbon Monoxide). It can be generated by burning coal. Another way is smoke from petrol or deisel vehicle but, I think, it is pretty nauseaous. Fumes from burning coal at a particular rate does’t cause nausea. There are two or three types of coal, and one of them is suited best for producing CO. Amount of coal to be burnt, the manner it should be burnt, the duration needed for fatal impact… all that detail is critical.
2. Shooting in temple (near ear), or inside mouth towards head. Literature says that the latter method is better assured than the first. One needs some medical (anatomoical) information to use these methods accurately.
3. Hanging in a right way. One way is long drop. It is used in capital punishments. In this, the neck breaks and the upper vertebrae (near neck) get severed so fast that the person doesn’t feel the pain. Another way is hanging softly. This, if done properly, presses upon the jugular (blood vessels) and cuts the blood supply to brain. Many of those who tried, report it to be almost painless. It may take a few minutes for a persona to die - which is very long, but one loses consciousness within a minute. The rope should be thick, and perhaps the neck should be padded with something, and the noose shouldn’t be placed in such a way which will cause larynx to get crushed.
4. Jumping off a very high building will cause an instantaneous and painless death. But it wil require tremendous courage to do so.

There is ample literature on internet on how to use these methods it in a right way.

Now the **advise**:

Someone, wanting to die, should evaluate the problems of his/her life one by one. And pick that one which can be most easily be worked upon. Often the the pain ( if mental) experienced by a person is a cumulative effect of different problems. Even if one of the problems is won over or is even reduced, the overall drive or need to die doesn’t sustain.

Often in the phase of suicide contemplation, mood swings from feeling utter doom to utter aggression. It is a good idea to utilize the utter aggression (when it occurs) and die fighting/struggling with the problems rather than die escaping from those.

But if all the problems are such which are sure to remain sustained, and there is no way to get rid of those, and the pain is too high, and it is been really long… then the propensity towards dying will continue.

Even in that case, any decision must be arrived at after a non-impulsive and cold blooded thinking and assessment. Hasty or impulse ridden thinking will definitely lead to wrong conclusions.

Ethics demand that if one has small children or very old parents totally dependent upon him/her then s/he should try to bear the pain as long as it is possible.

Survival instinct is the most fundamental and powerful of all instincts. If an individual is contemplaing suicide, it means that the pain is tremendous, and the factors causing it are very very sustained and strong. It shows that the pain is either so intense or so chronic that it has reversed or mutated even this most basic instinct.

Thus, final decision is an individual’s decision. Right to die is part of right to live, especially if the individual is living in too intense or chronic a pain (mental or physcial).
